newsitem.title: FINLAND: SAMPO TARGETS 15 PERCENT EPS GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: SAMPO TARGETS 15 PERCENT EPS GROWTH.

text.p: Finnish insurer Sampo targets 15 percent growth in earnings per share, CEO Jouko Leskinen told a news conference on Wednesday.
"We are targetting at a 15 percent annual growth (in EPS)," Leskinen said. Sampo said in a statement earlier that it planned to continue paying out at least a third of profits in dividends.
Sampo's 1996 EPS was 16.1 markka -- up from 11.8 in 1995 -- and the dividend was raised to six markka from five.
Leskinen said the bourse gains this year had exceeded Sampo's expectations and that group was satisfied with the current level of the HEX general index.

Asked to comment on the prospects for life-insurance which was consolidated from the beginning of 1997, and its impact on group earnings, he said: "The result impact will not be significant during the first couple of years but it will be clearly positive."
